title: Introduction: The AI Compute Spectrum (CPU, GPU, TPU, NPU) - Workload Breakdown: Why AI Needs Parallel Matrix Math
text: Hey, I'm Muskin. CPU, GPU, TPU, NPU, it's alphabet soup. But there's a simple idea underneath. AI does mostly one kind of math, and these chips are just different bets on how to do it fast. Let me give you a lens that makes all four make sense. Start with the workload. Normal computing is a few complex steps done in order. That's what a CPU is great at. But AI is different. It's billions of tiny multiply and adds, the same simple math over and over. To be fast, you don't want one clever core, you want to do enormous amounts of it at once. That's the whole story. AI is parallel matrix math. So here are the four. A CPU has a few powerful cores and runs everything. A GPU has thousands of simpler cores built for parallel math. It's the workhorse of AI.

title: The 4 Chips Explained: CPU, GPU, TPU, & NPU
text: A TPU is a custom chip built specifically for tensor math. And an NPU is a small, low-power one that runs AI right on your device. Line them up and you get a spectrum from general to specialized. The CPU does anything. The GPU is faster at AI, but less flexible. The TPU and NPU are faster still, but they only do a narrow job.
